cards.front: Which British Act designated the Governor of Bengal as the 'Governor-General of Bengal', and who was the first to hold this office?
cards.back: Regulating Act of 1773. Lord Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General of Bengal, assisted by an Executive Council of four members.
cards.key_fact: Regulating Act 1773 created Governor-General of Bengal (Lord Warren Hastings).

cards.front: Under which Act was the Supreme Court established at Fort William in Calcutta, and who was its first Chief Justice?
cards.back: Regulating Act of 1773 (established in 1774). Sir Elijah Impey was appointed as the first Chief Justice, accompanied by three other judges.
cards.key_fact: Supreme Court at Calcutta established in 1774 under Regulating Act 1773.

cards.front: Which Act established the system of 'Double Government' by separating commercial and political functions between the Court of Directors and Board of Control?
cards.back: Pitt's India Act of 1784. The Court of Directors managed commercial affairs, while the newly created Board of Control supervised civil, military, and revenue affairs.
cards.key_fact: Pitt's India Act 1784 established Double Government with the Board of Control.

cards.front: Under which enactment were the Company's territories in India referred to for the very first time as 'British possessions in India'?
cards.back: Pitt's India Act of 1784. It asserted the British Crown's supreme control over Company administration in India.
cards.key_fact: Pitt's India Act 1784 first used the term 'British possessions in India'.

cards.front: Which Charter Act mandated that the salaries and expenses of the Board of Control and their staff be paid out of Indian revenues?
cards.back: Charter Act of 1793. This initiated the financial drain known as 'Home Charges' from Indian revenues.
cards.key_fact: Charter Act 1793 charged Board of Control expenses to Indian revenues.

cards.front: Which Charter Act abolished the East India Company's trade monopoly with India, except for the trade in tea and trade with China?
cards.back: Charter Act of 1813. It threw open Indian trade to all British merchants while preserving the Company's monopoly over tea and China trade for 20 more years.
cards.key_fact: Charter Act 1813 ended Indian trade monopoly except tea and China trade.

cards.front: Which Act allocated an annual grant of Rs 1 Lakh for education and literature, and permitted Christian missionaries to enter India?
cards.back: Charter Act of 1813. It allocated Rs 1,00,000 for the revival and promotion of literature and encouragement of learned natives of India (PYQ-0925).
cards.key_fact: Charter Act 1813 allocated Rs 1 Lakh for education and permitted missionaries.

cards.front: Which Act created the office of 'Governor-General of India' with exclusive civil and military powers, and who was the first Governor-General of India?
cards.back: Charter Act of 1833. Lord William Bentinck was appointed as the first Governor-General of India.
cards.key_fact: Charter Act 1833 created Governor-General of India (Lord William Bentinck).

cards.front: Which Act completely ended all commercial activities of the East India Company (including tea and trade with China), making it a purely administrative body?
cards.back: Charter Act of 1833. It extinguished all remaining commercial monopolies, rendering the Company a trustee for the Crown.
cards.key_fact: Charter Act 1833 completely ended EIC commercial operations.

cards.front: Who was added as the fourth member (Law Member) to the Governor-General's Council under the Charter Act of 1833?
cards.back: Lord Thomas Babington Macaulay was appointed as the first Law Member (without voting power in executive matters), leading to the First Law Commission (1834).
cards.key_fact: Charter Act 1833 added Law Member (Lord Macaulay) to Governor-General's Council.

cards.front: Which Act separated the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's Council by creating a 6-member Indian Legislative Council?
cards.back: Charter Act of 1853. It established the Indian (Central) Legislative Council, functioning as a mini-parliament on the British model.
cards.key_fact: Charter Act 1853 separated executive and legislative wings of Governor-General's Council.

cards.front: Which Act introduced an open competition system for the selection and recruitment of civil servants, leading to the Macaulay Committee of 1854?
cards.back: Charter Act of 1853. The Committee on the Indian Civil Service (Macaulay Committee) was appointed in 1854 to implement open competitive examinations.
cards.key_fact: Charter Act 1853 introduced open competition for civil services (Macaulay Committee 1854).

cards.front: Which Act is titled the 'Act for the Better Government of India', and what was its core constitutional effect?
cards.back: Government of India Act 1858. It abolished East India Company rule following the 1857 revolt and transferred sovereignty, territories, and revenues directly to the British Crown.
cards.key_fact: GoI Act 1858 transferred Indian governance from Company to British Crown.

cards.front: Which two major administrative offices were created by the Government of India Act 1858 to replace the Board of Control and Court of Directors?
cards.back: The Viceroy of India (Lord Canning was first) as direct Crown representative, and the Secretary of State for India in London, assisted by a 15-member Council of India.
cards.key_fact: GoI Act 1858 created Viceroy (Lord Canning) and Secretary of State for India.

cards.front: Which Act initiated legislative decentralization by restoring law-making powers to Bombay and Madras Presidencies, and recognized the Portfolio system?
cards.back: Indian Councils Act of 1861. It reversed the centralization trend of 1833 and legalized the Portfolio system introduced by Lord Canning in 1859.
cards.key_fact: Indian Councils Act 1861 initiated decentralization and legalized the Portfolio system.

cards.front: Which three Indian non-official members were nominated to the Viceroy's Legislative Council by Lord Canning under the Indian Councils Act 1861?
cards.back: The Raja of Benaras, the Maharaja of Patiala, and Sir Dinkar Rao were nominated in 1862.
cards.key_fact: 1861 Councils Act nominated Raja of Benaras, Maharaja of Patiala, and Sir Dinkar Rao.

cards.front: Which Act empowered legislative council members to discuss the annual budget and address questions to the executive for the first time?
cards.back: Indian Councils Act of 1892. It expanded legislative functions, though members could not vote on the budget or ask supplementary questions (PYQ-0520).
cards.key_fact: Indian Councils Act 1892 granted powers to discuss budget and question executive.

cards.front: Which Act introduced communal representation (separate electorates) for Muslims, and who became known as the 'Father of Communal Electorate'?
cards.back: Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms). Lord Minto (Viceroy) came to be known as the Father of Communal Electorate (PYQ-0758, PYQ-3073).
cards.key_fact: 1909 Morley-Minto Reforms introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

cards.front: What were the 'Reserved' versus 'Transferred' subjects under the Dyarchy system introduced by the Government of India Act 1919?
cards.back: Reserved subjects (Police, Land Revenue, Justice) were administered by Governor + Executive Council without assembly accountability. Transferred subjects (Local Self-Govt, Health, Education) were administered by Governor with elected Ministers (PYQ-0690, PYQ-0759).
cards.key_fact: 1919 Act introduced provincial Dyarchy with Reserved (Police/Revenue) and Transferred (Local Self-Govt) lists.

cards.front: Which Act introduced 'Provincial Autonomy', divided powers into Federal, Provincial, and Concurrent Lists, and where did it vest residuary powers?
cards.back: Government of India Act of 1935. It abolished provincial dyarchy, granted autonomy to provinces, divided powers into 3 lists, and vested residuary powers in the Governor-General (Viceroy).
cards.key_fact: GoI Act 1935 introduced Provincial Autonomy, 3 Lists, and vested residuary powers in the Viceroy.
